correctness.rationale: Direct expansion of the mixed compatibility identity forces \(r=c\), \(s=-b\), \(g=-c\), and \(d=-b\). The residual pre-Lie equations are exactly \(b(a+b+c-h)=c(a+b+c-h)=0\), so over a field the solution set is \(H\cup P\) with dimensions three and two and line intersection. The fixed first algebra has only the identity and the basis swap as automorphisms; the swap fixed locus is the affine plane \(a=h\), \(c=-b\). Inclusion-exclusion and Burnside then give the stated counts. The packaged exhaustive checker verifies the defining identities and orbit partitions over three finite fields, including characteristic two.

value.rationale: The first product \(K\times K\) is the canonical semisimple two-dimensional algebra, so its compatible-product fiber is a natural base case rather than an arbitrary slice. The result turns the complex family list into a field-uniform geometric decomposition, shows that characteristic two creates no extra field-valued branch, and gives exact finite-field moduli counts and orbit sizes. These counts are reusable baseline data for any finite-field classification or degeneration study of compatible pre-Lie structures.
